description: Fig. 7 is a four-panel set of grey-scale SEM micrographs of Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr low-density steel strips after annealing at 550 °C for 5 h; each panel carries the same 20 µm scale bar in its lower-right corner and a white panel label, with no magnification value or accelerating voltage printed. (a) 0Cr shows a fully dendritic/cellular surface: closely packed rosette-like or flower-shaped dendrites with radiating arms, deep inter-dendritic grooves and clearly resolvable grain boundaries and dendritic structure. (b) 3Cr, (c) 6Cr and (d) 9Cr instead show a smooth grey matrix in which numerous darker, sharply outlined second-phase particles are dispersed; these appear as fine dots and short elongated or angular fragments (b), more irregular and branched outlines (c), and coarser, blockier angular shapes (d). No continuous grain boundary or dendritic network is resolvable in the Cr-containing panels. Taken together the panels argue that a 5 h anneal at 550 °C leaves the 0Cr strip with a visible dendritic/grain-boundary structure while Cr additions of 3, 6 and 9 wt% suppress that visible boundary network and leave only dispersed second-phase particles. No composition or property values are printed.

observations.observation: All four panels are back-grey-scale SEM images of the same type with an identical 20 µm scale bar in the lower-right corner; no magnification or voltage is printed.
Panel (a) (0Cr) shows a fully dendritic morphology of packed rosette-like dendrites with radiating arms and deep inter-dendritic grooves.
In panel (a) the grain boundaries and dendritic structure are clearly visible, whereas no continuous grain boundary can be resolved by eye in panels (b), (c) or (d).
Panels (b) 3Cr, (c) 6Cr and (d) 9Cr show a smooth grey matrix containing dispersed darker second-phase particles with sharp outlines.
The dispersed dark particles become progressively coarser and more angular from (b) through (c) to (d), with (b) dominated by fine dots and short fragments and (d) by blockier angular shapes.
The caption states the images are SEM pictures of Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr low-density steel strips after annealing at 550 °C for 5 h, with (a) 0Cr, (b) 3Cr, (c) 6Cr and (d) 9Cr.
The citing text states that the constituent phases of the annealed Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr strips are still austenite and ferrite.

The citing text states that the (111) diffraction peak of κ-carbides at 41.4° appears in the annealed 0Cr strip but is not observed in Cr-containing annealed strips, so Cr suppresses κ-carbide precipitation even after annealing (XRD evidence from Fig. 6, not shown here).
The citing text interprets the absence of visible grain boundaries in the Cr-containing strips as evidence that Cr addition improves the corrosion resistance of the strips.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of annealed 0Cr strip: closely packed rosette/flower-like dendrites with radiating arms and prominent inter-dendritic grooves; grain boundaries and dendritic structure clearly visible. 20 µm scale bar at lower right.

SEM micrograph of annealed 3Cr strip: smooth grey matrix containing numerous small dark second-phase particles, mostly fine dots plus short elongated/angular fragments; no clear grain boundary. 20 µm scale bar.

SEM micrograph of annealed 6Cr strip: grey matrix with dispersed dark particles of more irregular, branched and skeleton-like outlines, plus small dotted particles; no resolvable grain boundary. 20 µm scale bar.
SEM micrograph of annealed 9Cr strip: grey matrix with coarser, blockier and angular dark second-phase particles dispersed throughout; grain boundaries not resolvable. 20 µm scale bar.
